channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Genetics, Cell Genomics, Genome Biology, Genome Research, Nucleic Acids Research, and RNA.

item.title: Genome Biology: Single-nucleus proteomics reveals proteins regulating LPS-induced nucleocytoplasmic transport in macrophages
Nucleic Acids Research: Disease-responsive promoters enable precisely controlled gene therapy
item.description: Abstract Adeno associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene therapy holds great promise for curing various diseases, but uncontrolled expression of transgenes in both healthy and diseased cells driven by constitutively active general promoters is a potential safety risk. Controlled gene therapy can be achieved using a disease-responsive promoter (DRP) that drives expression of a therapeutic gene only in diseased cells and shuts off once the cells become healthy again. We used correlative analysis of ATAC-seq and ncRNA-seq of healthy and diseased retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) to identify and characterize two DRPs that possess unique DRP activities in two mouse models of optic neuropathy. We further optimized one DRP to generate DRP-3L2, which has minimum promoter activity in naïve healthy RGCs, but drives potent neuroprotective gene expression in diseased RGCs and then abates after RGCs are protected and returning to health. Our proof-of-concept studies demonstrate that DRP-mediated precisely controlled gene therapy provides a new and promising neuroprotective strategy for CNS axonopathies.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: RNA fine-tunes KAT5 activity to shape chromatin acetylation during active transcription
item.description: Abstract KAT5 is a prominent histone acetyltransferase that deposits acetylation on histone H4 to regulate transcription, genome stability, and cell fate decisions. Although the chromatin recruitment of KAT5 and its associated NuA4/TIP60 complex is well characterized, the molecular mechanisms that regulate its catalytic activity are still largely unknown. Here, we identify RNA as a direct and reversible modulator of KAT5 activity. Using single-end enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (seCLIP-seq), we find that KAT5 binds RNA in cells with a strong preference for GC-rich mRNA sequences enriched near transcription start sites. Unexpectedly, loss of KAT5–RNA interactions during acute transcriptional inhibition triggers rapid and pronounced promoter hyperacetylation. Biochemical and structural analyses suggest that RNA engages an RNA-sensing autoinhibitory region within the HAT domain, sterically blocking substrate access to the catalytic pocket and thereby suppressing KAT5 acetyltransferase activity. Our findings uncover nascent RNA as a reversible allosteric inhibitor of KAT5, revealing an RNA-directed feedback mechanism that modulates promoter acetylation and gene expression.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Differential co-localization analysis of multi-sample and multi-condition experiments with spatialFDA
item.description: Abstract Advances in spatial omics data generation have led to an explosion in new datasets that record the spatial location of transcripts and proteins. However, challenges remain in the analysis of spatial omics data. One important analysis is differential cellular co-localization (CCoL): the quantification of the clustering, or spacing, of one or more cell types across multiple conditions. Our framework spatialFDA combines methodology from spatial statistics with functional data analysis to accurately quantify and test for differences between conditions in CCoL across spatial scales. Using two simulation studies, we show that spatialFDA performs well in controlled settings. Furthermore, spatialFDA recovers known biological processes in type-1 diabetes and adds insights about the CCoL strength in space. spatialFDA is readily available as an open-source Bioconductor R package.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Nicking Loop™: streamlined circular DNA libraries for precise targeted sequencing and universal NGS read-out
item.description: Abstract Circular single-stranded DNA (CssDNA) offers unique advantages for molecular diagnostics and next-generation sequencing (NGS) due to its nuclease degradation resistance and compatibility with rolling circle amplification. CssDNA is used with several modern NGS platforms, but many library preparation workflows require a conversion step involving splinting and an enzymatic treatment, adding workflow complexity. This study introduces Nicking Loop™, a targeted library preparation method that converts single- and double-stranded DNA into CssDNA, enabling direct circular sequencing and controlled linear amplification that can be repeated over multiple generations. The method demonstrated improved preservation of variant allele frequencies across three amplification generations compared to PCR, which is particularly relevant for detection of low-abundance variants. Sequencing of Nicking Loop™ circular libraries on Pacific Biosciences Onso™ platform demonstrated direct compatibility without additional library conversion steps. Nicking Loop™ is compatible with consensus sequencing for Oxford Nanopore, highlighting its applicability across multiple NGS platforms. Furthermore, Nicking Loop™ introduces a loop-based indexing strategy that enables early sample indexing for parallel processing of multiple samples. This proof-of-concept demonstrates the feasibility of Nicking Loop™ library preparation across multiple NGS platforms, contributing to the growing adoption of circular NGS platforms for applications requiring sensitive and accurate detection of low-abundance targets.

item.title: Nature Genetics: A draft mouse pangenome graph reference
item.description: Three base-level graph-based mouse pangenomes built on the C57BL/6J mouse telomere-to-telomere backbone provide resources for improved alignment, reduced reference bias, more accurate variant calling and downstream functional genomics.

Genome Biology: FOXK2 lactylation drives sorafenib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma by activating fatty acid oxidation
Genome Biology: The structure-specific endonuclease HIGLE contributes to TONSOKU-mediated DNA repair during replication in Arabidopsis thaliana
Nucleic Acids Research: Rapid degradation of six class I HDAC complexes reveals a mixture of unique, cooperative, and antagonistic roles
item.description: Abstract The class I histone deacetylases (HDACs) 1, 2, and 3 form seven families of distinct large multiprotein complexes that regulate gene expression via deacetylation of lysines in histone tails. The degree of redundancy and functional overlap between complexes and their acute gene targets remain unknown. We used CRISPR/Cas9 to create six cell lines in which individual HDAC complexes were tagged with FKBP12 F36V enabling rapid (<1 h), PROTAC-mediated, degradation. RNA sequencing at 6 h reveals that together, the four major complexes (CoREST, NuRD, NCoR/SMRT, and SIN3A) perturbed >50% of expressed genes. More than 60% of these are regulated by a single complex. ChIP-sequencing revealed that >54% of differentially expressed genes are directly regulated by the associated complex. Of genes regulated by more than one complex, approaching 50% are reciprocally regulated such that HDAC complexes act as antagonistic regulators. Homer analysis strongly suggests that the complexes are reliant on different transcription factors. This is the first study to rapidly degrade individual HDAC complexes, and identify and compare their acute gene targets. Together, these results show HDAC complexes regulate specific gene sets with minimal overlap of gene regulation within the same biological system.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Translons upstream of protein-coding regions rather than their products are crucial for proliferation of human cells of distinct origin
item.description: Abstract Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are a widespread class of translated regions (translons) occurring in 5′ leaders of messenger RNAs. They serve critical roles in post-transcriptional regulation and some are known to encode small proteins and peptideins. Yet it is not known which of these modes of function is more critical for human cells. We conducted a CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis screening targeting 969 translated human uORFs across three cell lines of distinct origin. Disruption of 155 uORFs impaired cell proliferation, although these effects were highly cell-type specific, with only six shared across all cell lines. Neither evolutionary conservation, comparative protein-coding potential, nor population mutational constraint distinguished uORF hits. Instead, high-throughput analysis of CRISPR-induced mutations combined with reporter assays demonstrated that proliferation phenotypes arise from altered cis -regulation of coding sequence (CDS) translation. In particular, uORFs located within short 5′ leaders were disproportionately sensitive to indels, which frequently changed the uORF–CDS configuration, resulting in altered gene expression. We further identified naturally occurring human variants that are predicted to perturb these uORFs–CDS configurations, potentially contributing to disease phenotypes. Together, these findings identify uORF translation as a pervasive layer of gene-expression control. This study demonstrates that for most uORFs, it is their native translation rather than the activity of their products that is critical for the proliferation of human cells. It also provides a systematic resource for investigating uORF functions.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: AAV-mediated XIST deletion in female human hepatocytes with skewed X-inactivation induces limited reactivation of the X-linked OTC gene in vivo
item.description: Abstract Reactivation of silenced wild-type alleles on the inactive X chromosome (Xi) offers a promising therapeutic avenue for X-linked disorders affecting females. The long non-coding RNA XIST is central to Xi silencing, yet its complete loss risks chromosome-wide dosage imbalance. To explore reactivation in a translational context, we employed chimeric mouse–human FRG livers repopulated with primary hepatocytes from a female patient with ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency exhibiting highly skewed X-inactivation. Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated CRISPR–Cas9 delivery was used to disrupt XIST in vivo to assess effects on chromatin landscape and OTC expression. Despite differential XIST promoter methylation, the Xi remained accessible to CRISPR–Cas9, with editing frequencies comparable to those of the active X chromosome. XIST deletion induced limited reactivation of the wild-type OTC allele and was accompanied by broader epigenetic effects. CUT&RUN profiling distinguished effects of vector delivery and XIST deletion, including global H3K4me3 reduction after AAV transduction, X chromosome-restricted H3K27me3 reduction after XIST deletion, and broader H3K27ac reduction in edited hepatocytes. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of manipulating the human Xi in vivo while revealing distinct Xi-specific and broader chromatin effects. Together, they highlight the need for precise, locus-specific strategies to achieve therapeutic gene reactivation while preserving chromosome-wide epigenetic regulation.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Endogenous variability in transcription factor concentrations shapes their genome-wide occupancy
item.description: Abstract The control of transcription factor (TF) concentrations is crucial for the precise regulation of gene expression and cell fate decisions during development. Yet, TF concentrations can display substantial temporal fluctuations and intercellular variations. How TF levels quantitatively shape genome-wide occupancy patterns remains largely unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate how physiological fluctuations in the concentrations of the pluripotency TFs OCT4, SOX2, and NANOG impact their genomic binding profiles in mouse embryonic stem cells. We uncover distinct concentration-dependent binding behaviors for each TF. NANOG occupancy increased monotonously with its concentration, even though a common set of regions made accessible by OCT4 and SOX2 are highly and uniformly bound at all NANOG concentrations. In contrast, SOX2 occupancy does not increase with its concentrations, while OCT4 displayed an intermediate behavior. Our results challenge the notion that TF binding follows simple mass-action dynamics and reveal a core set of pluripotency regions that are bound by all three TFs at all TF concentrations, revealing how pluripotency can be maintained despite marked fluctuations in core pluripotency TFs.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Reprogramming mRNA localization by targeted RNA-protein interference reveals roles in oncogenesis
item.description: Abstract RNA binding proteins (RBPs) associate with RNAs in intricate ribonucleoprotein complexes and regulate various aspects of RNA life cycle and, by extension, cell functions. Despite their significance, elucidating the functional contributions of specific RNA–RBP binding events, particularly in long-term phenotypic assays, remains challenging. Here, we harness the specificity of CRISPR/dCas13 to interfere with specific RNA–RBP interactions. We apply this methodology to GA-rich mRNA localization elements which recruit the RNA-binding protein CNBP and serve as platforms for the assembly of mRNA trafficking complexes. We show that dCas13/gRNA binds to target transcripts in a highly specific manner and interferes with CNBP recruitment leading to altered target mRNA localization and cell motility, consistent with the function of the targeted mRNAs. We describe optimizations and considerations for the stable implementation of this system. We further use it to show that interfering with the localization of the GA-containing NET1 mRNA reduces cancer cell invasiveness and metastatic lung colonization. These data reveal a potential role for mRNA localization in oncogenic progression and illustrate how this CRISPR-based system can be used for long-term functional investigations of RNA–RBP interactions in vivo .

item.title: Genome Biology: Transposable element copy number variation reveals demographic and environment-associated dynamics during apple domestication
Nature Genetics: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
item.description: Multiancestry genome-wide association coupled with integrative multiomics analyses identify risk loci for endometriosis and implicate key genes and pathways underlying its pathogenesis, including roles for immune cell types and cellular proliferation.

item.title: Genome Biology: Korea10K integrates 10,239 whole genomes with multiomic and clinical health information as a Korean reference dataset
Nature Genetics: Optimizing phenotype scale improves genetic analyses in large-scale biobanks
item.description: SIQReg is a data-driven approach for optimizing phenotype scale transformation that substantially reduces scale-dependent heterogeneity while preserving biologically plausible nonadditive signals and improving power to detect additive signals.

item.title: Genome Biology: Benchmarking computational tools for locus-specific analysis of transposable elements in single-cell RNA-seq datasets
Genome Biology: Dynamic changes in mRNA isoform usage during human retinal organoid development
Genome Biology: Naturally occurring variation in gene-associated transposable elements impacts gene expression and phenotypic diversity in woodland strawberry
Genome Biology: Inherent specificity and variation sensitivity as quantitative metrics for RNA binding proteins
Nature Genetics: Regularized ensemble polygenic risk prediction with GWAS summary statistics
item.description: PUMAS-ensemble combines multiple polygenic risk scores using genome-wide association study summary statistics, improving genetic risk prediction across traits and ancestry groups without requiring individual-level training data.

item.title: Genome Biology: Pennycress population genomics reveals a complex global expansion history and local climate-adaptation targets for neodomestication
Nature Genetics: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
item.description: This study presents a scalable framework for understanding the genetic determinants of gene expression and cellular phenotype in stem-cell-derived microglia-like cells and linking these to neurodegenerative disease.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Evolutionary lineage-specific and heterochromatin-independent repression of transposon-derived sequences
item.description: This study identifies SCAN zinc-finger proteins as rapidly evolving transcription factors that target lineage-specific transposable elements and restrict their regulatory activity without canonical repressive chromatin modifications.

item.title: Genome Biology: Integrating hyperspectral phenomics and genome-wide association analysis reveals a ribosome assembly factor regulating wheat grain protein content under drought stress
Nature Genetics: High-quality pig pan-genome resources illuminate centromere evolution and enhance genotype–phenotype mapping
item.description: Pig genomic resources comprising 3 telomere-to-telomere genomes and 16 chromosome-level assemblies, integrated with transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles, highlight centromere evolution and facilitate genotype–phenotype mapping.

item.title: Cell Genomics: The Drosophila melanogaster Genetic Reference Panel version 3
item.description: The Drosophila melanogaster Genetic Reference Panel version 3 (DGRP3) expands a widely used community resource to over 1,000 sequenced inbred lines. Harboring 8.7 million polymorphisms, this population and its companion mapping tool enable high-resolution genome-wide association mapping of quantitative traits in this genetic model organism.

item.title: Genome Biology: Human astrocyte aging couples chromatin closure to focal G-quadruplex accumulation
Cell Genomics: RNA sequencing reveals molecular subtypes across adenocarcinoma, squamous, and small cell lung cancer
item.description: Arora et al. integrate gene expression profiles from 1,824 lung tumors to create a unified landscape of lung cancer. The map reveals nine transcriptional states spanning traditional diagnoses; highlights distinct lineage, immune, and metabolic programs; and provides a reference for comparing patient tumors with experimental models.

item.title: Cell Genomics: Distinct extraembryonic transcription factors converge on a shared DNA methylation-Polycomb state
item.description: Haggerty et al. define a developmental window during which chromatin can be rapidly and globally reprogrammed between two distinct epigenetic landscapes and indicate that key features of the extraembryonic and cancer epigenomes can be explained as differences in epigenetic regulation, rather than passive mechanisms like epigenetic drift or incomplete gain.

item.title: Genome Biology: G-quadruplex profiling using single-cell CUT&Tag offers insight into the epigenetic landscape of the developing mouse brain
Genome Biology: Structure-guided engineering of eukaryotic Fanzor-ωRNA system enhances in vivo gene editing for dystrophin restoration in a Duchenne mouse model
Cell Genomics: Amyloid and tau display distinct patterns across Alzheimer’s in anterior caudate
item.description: Kana et al. built a single-nucleus and spatial atlas of the anterior caudate across Alzheimer’s disease. Caudate pathology is mainly diffuse amyloid-β plaques and white matter tau threads. Despite no neuronal loss, they find an increase in FLT1+/IL1B+ microglial state with vascular signaling and altered gene expression in fast-spiking interneurons.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Saturation genome editing of BRCA1 across cell types improves interpretation of variant pathogenicity
item.description: Saturation genome editing maps the functional effects of thousands of BRCA1 variants across two complementary cell models. Discordantly scored variants reflect the importance of context and provide insights for improving BRCA1 variant interpretation.

item.title: Cell Genomics: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis identifies susceptibility loci informing Ewing sarcoma etiology and potential mechanisms of risk
item.description: Hubbard et al. perform a genome-wide association meta-analysis combined with a case-parent trio study to identify 14 Ewing sarcoma susceptibility loci. Most loci contain GGAA microsatellites bound by the tumor-defining EWSR1::FLI1 fusion protein, highlighting interplay between inherited genetic variation and somatically acquired oncogenic fusions in Ewing sarcoma.

item.title: Genome Biology: Spatial transcriptomics defines segmental and temporal dynamics of pig intestinal epithelium
Nature Genetics: Efficient count-based models improve power and robustness for large-scale single-cell eQTL mapping
item.description: This study presents jaxQTL, an efficient count-based pseudobulk single-cell eQTL mapping framework. When applied to OneK1K data, jaxQTL discovers more eGenes than existing methods while running faster.

item.title: Genome Biology: Short-read sequencing benchmarking with donor-specific assemblies
Nature Genetics: A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
item.description: This study presents SheepGTEx, a comprehensive multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory variants derived from 6,761 samples across 51 tissues, providing insights into complex traits, population selection and domestication history in sheep.

item.title: Genome Biology: Community benchmarking of generative models for privacy-preserving synthetic bulk RNA-seq data generation
Nature Genetics: Efficient and accurate mixed model association tool for single-cell eQTL analysis
item.description: SAIGE-QTL is a framework for eQTL mapping that directly models single-cell read counts using a Poisson mixed model, achieving improved statistical efficiency and power and enabling rare variant set-based testing in the single-cell eQTL setting.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch
item.description: RSparsePro performs robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch by coupling a probabilistic graphical model with a variational inference algorithm, identifying credible sets with higher power and coverage than existing methods.

item.title: Nature Genetics: An information-theoretic framework for inferring T cell dynamics from single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing
item.description: T cells provide a unique setting for quantification of the relationship between genotype and phenotype. The authors introduce TCRi, an information-theoretic framework for this, and find mutual information to be a robust determinant of immunotherapeutic response.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Multiscale multimodal integration of spatial omics through a deep generative model with CORAL
item.description: Cross-scale spatial Omics Registration and Analysis via graph Learning is a deep generative model that integrates multiscale spatial multi-omics data using graph-attention aggregation mechanisms, enabling a comprehensive spatial analysis.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors
item.description: This longitudinal single-cell study of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer suggests that strong estrogen signaling, ER-linked enhancers and active T cell responses could predict sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors, whereas resistance involves androgen signaling though hormone-sensing enhancer activity.

item.title: Nature Genetics: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction
item.description: This study introduces a framework for integrating DNA methylation data across more than 90 tissues and cell types, characterizing genome-wide methylation patterns and predicting context-specific effects of genetic variants on DNA methylation and regulatory function using a deep learning model, Wreath.

item.title: Nature Genetics: AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization for childhood brain tumors
item.description: Stefan et al. present MANTIS, an AI model to predict individualized survival in childhood brain tumors from routine DNA methylation profiling. MANTIS may help identify patients who benefit from less intense treatment to reduce lifelong side effects.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy
item.description: This study shows that clonal hematopoiesis expands after chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy and contributes to secondary myeloid cancers. In addition, the CAR vector frequently integrates into pre-existing clonal hematopoiesis.

item.title: Nature Genetics: A catalog of transcriptome genetic regulation in a consanguineous Middle Eastern biobank
item.description: This study reports an atlas of transcriptomic genetic effects from a Middle Eastern population biobank, revealing population-specific regulatory variants and links to clinically relevant traits.

item.title: Genome Biology: Comprehensive evaluation of antibody language models across multiple antibody design tasks
Genome Biology: Telomere-to-telomere genome of a dodecaploid desert shrub Prunus pedunculata reveals polyploidy-driven arid adaptation
Nature Genetics: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation
item.description: Single-nucleus chromatin accessibility and transcriptome maps of human skeletal muscle identify cell-state and context-specific QTLs that colocalize with genome-wide association signals for cardiometabolic traits.

item.title: Genome Biology: Chemogenomic profiling of diverse Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains using the novel CRISPR-Cas9 markerless barcoded library BarMix
Cell Genomics: TFXcan reveals transcription factor programs driving GWAS loci
item.description: Adeluwa et al. developed TFXcan, a framework that predicts personalized transcription factor binding from genotype data across ∼700 transcription-factor-tissue pairs. Applied to PrCa risk, TFXcan identified specific transcription factors and coordinated programs of transcription factors that drive the disease at risk loci.

item.title: Genome Biology: The glutamine-aspartate metabolic tradeoff between fast growth and metabolic flexibility
Genome Biology: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
Genome Biology: Mitonuclear control of transcription complexes regulates tRNA splicing
Cell Genomics: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer
item.description: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection

item.title: Genome Biology: A new phased assembly of the Antarctic spiny plunderfish provides novel insights into the evolution of the notothenioid radiation
Cell Genomics: Choice of phenotype scale is critical in biobank-based G × E tests
item.description: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.
